{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. Of the nineteen rules assessed, twelve clauses are compliant, six are deviations, and one required clause is missing. All findings below are verified.

The risk-allocation core of the agreement is strong and should be protected in negotiation: Vendor indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14–15), the mutual liability cap with Excluded Claims sitting outside it (§ 21), assignment and change-of-control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), warranties and remedies (§ 19), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), insurance (§ 18), governing law and venue (§ 28), and the express no-minimum-commitment and no-non-compete confirmations (§ 2.1, § 12.3).

The problems cluster in a small number of one-way commercial restraints imposed on us, several of which contradict § 12.3 (in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment). Specifically: full-term exclusive dealing (§ 2.2), a Customer-payable daily liquidated damages penalty (§ 7.6), an open-ended MFN running against us (§ 7.2), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), unlimited unannounced audits with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1), and a one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-hire (§ 12.4). In addition, the agreement contains **no Customer termination-for-convenience right** against a three-year initial term with automatic 12-month renewals. Five of these items sit in walk-away territory under the playbook.

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with 20.2–20.5) | Meets preferred position; indemnities are Excluded Claims under § 21.3, better than the 3× super-cap fallback. No redline. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) | Meets preferred position. Note only: draft Order Forms to capture all bespoke work product within the § 1.4 "Deliverable" definition. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full Excluded Claims list. Preferred position. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Meets preferred position in full; no change-of-control trigger elsewhere. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Full-term sole-and-exclusive provider commitment, no category narrowing, no 12-month limit, no performance exit — walk-away. **Delete § 2.2**; offer fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on missed service levels) if commercially necessary. Also contradicts § 2.1 and § 12.3. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day for "any delay in providing a dependency", uncapped and with no materiality threshold — walk-away. **Delete and substitute equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as sole remedy**; fallback is a single amount capped at three months' fees. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with 13.2–13.4, 14.3) | Meets preferred position; no at-will revocation right. No redline. |
| High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | MFN runs against us, open-ended as to product, term and comparators — walk-away, and contradicts § 12.3. **Delete the Customer-side MFN.** |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-compete binding us; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom of action and should be retained. Exclusivity is addressed under EXCLUSIVITY only. |
| High | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 (pricing limb § 8.3) | 180-day non-renewal notice is double the 90-day walk-away threshold and beyond the 60-day fallback. **Shorten to 30 days and add a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal**; 60 days available as fallback. Renewal uplift cap in § 8.3 already meets preferred position. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 TERMINATION | Only for-cause, insolvency and specific-trigger rights exist against a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals — walk-away. **Add new § 9.4: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee, and no reciprocal Vendor right**; 60 days available as fallback. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote access to our systems — walk-away, and contradicts § 22.2. **Limit to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, no system access.** Cost allocation (§ 22.2) and confidentiality of findings (§ 22.3) already meet preferred position. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with 28.2–28.3) | New York law and exclusive New York County venue; no arbitration provision. Preferred position. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with 7.1, 12.3) | Express disclaimer of minimum quantity or purchase commitment; no take-or-pay or shortfall penalty. Preferred position. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way, 18 months post-termination, any Vendor employee at any time during the term, extends to "engage" (effective no-hire), no general-advertising carve-out; fails the fallback on every material term and conflicts with § 12.3. **Delete § 12.4**; narrow mutual fallback offered in comment. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with 11.2–11.3, 10.1–10.2) | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; data return within 30 days, no withholding over fee disputes; deletion only after confirmed return. Preferred position. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with 19.2–19.5) | Full warranty ladder; hosted-Services conformance warranty for the whole subscription term; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. Preferred position. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with 18.2) | Meets or exceeds every preferred limit; insurance does not cap Vendor liability. Runs in our favour. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 2.2 — Full-term exclusivity.** Sole-and-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the whole term, with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no service-level or delivery-failure exit.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any delay in providing a dependency, uncapped and with no materiality threshold; the § 21.1 mutual cap does not cure it, as exposure can still reach 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000.
3. **§ 7.2 — Open-ended MFN against us.** No defined product or service, no time limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access.**
5. **Absence of a Customer termination-for-convenience right** across a three-year initial term with automatic 12-month renewals (§ 8.1, § 8.2, § 9).

Also close to the line: the **no-hire element of § 12.4** (extension to "engage", covering any Vendor employee at any time during the term).

We note that items 1, 3 and the § 12.4 restraint each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3, which strengthens our position that these are deletions rather than negotiations.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven action items: delete § 2.2, § 7.2, § 7.6 (replaced with equitable schedule relief as Vendor's sole remedy) and § 12.4; amend § 8.2 (30-day window plus 60-day Vendor reminder) and § 22.1 (annual, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor, no system access); and insert new § 9.4 (convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund and no reciprocal Vendor right).
2. **Confirm the commercial line** with the business owner on exclusivity: if any exclusivity is genuinely required, we table the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on missed service levels) rather than accept § 2.2 as drafted.
3. **Set the fallback envelope** for negotiation: 60 days on both the non-renewal window and the convenience-notice period; a single capped early-termination amount (three months' fees) if Vendor insists on a monetary construct in place of § 7.6.
4. **Protect the compliant provisions.** Flag § 12.3, § 2.1, § 20, § 21, § 24 and § 11 as no-change items and resist reciprocal concessions being extracted against them.
5. **Operational follow-up on scope.** Ensure Order Forms are drafted so that all bespoke work product falls within the § 1.4 "Deliverable" definition, and note for the finance team that the § 1.5 "Fees" definition excludes one-time implementation charges unless an Order Form states otherwise.
6. **Return to the deal team** with Vendor's response for a go/no-go assessment on the walk-away items before signature."}
